candidates.exact_span:
a. The permittee shall test the effluent for toxicity in accordance with the provisions in this
      section.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a mandatory toxicity-testing obligation; interpreting which effluent, which outfalls, and which provisions govern frequency or triggering conditions changes whether monitoring was required for FY2025.

Scopes toxicity requirements to final outfall 001; a different reading of outfall applicability would change which discharge points receive limit comparisons, monitoring obligations, and missing-evidence evaluations.

Sets the dilution level used to judge chronic lethal and sub-lethal failure; interpreting 100% critical dilution changes the concentration at which reported toxicity results are compared for compliance.

Defines the test dilution series used to determine NOEC and failure; different interpretation of which dilutions must be tested or how results at these levels map to pass/fail could change limit-exceedance determinations.

candidates.exact_span:
TEST SPECIES AND METHODS           Ceriodaphnia dubia / Method 1002.0 (EPA-
                                    821-R-02-013 or latest version)
                                    Pimephales promelas/ Method 1000.0
                                    (EPA/821/R-02-013 or latest version)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies required species and EPA methods (including 'latest version' language); interpreting which method version or species applies changes whether monitoring was required and whether reported or missing results satisfy the obligation.

candidates.exact_span: SAMPLE TYPE                        Defined in PART I
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defers sample-type requirements to PART I; resolving that cross-reference changes what sampling was required and how absent or nonconforming sample types are classified for missing-evidence semantics.

candidates.exact_span:
b. The NOEC (No Observed Lethal Effect Concentration) is herein defined as the greatest
      effluent dilution at and below which lethality that is statistically different from the control
      (0% effluent) at the 95% confidence level does not occur.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines the pass/fail metric for lethal toxicity; interpretation of NOEC, statistical significance at 95% confidence, and 'greatest dilution' could change whether a reported measurement is treated as within or exceeding the applicable limit.

candidates.exact_span:
Chronic lethal test failure is
      defined as a demonstration of a statistically significant lethal effect at test completion to a
      test species at or below the critical dilution.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes when a lethal toxicity test constitutes failure; different readings of 'statistically significant', 'at test completion', or 'at or below the critical dilution' would change exceedance determinations.

candidates.exact_span:
Chronic sub-lethal test failure is defined as a
      demonstration of a statistically significant sub-lethal effect (i.e., growth or reproduction)
      at test completion to a test species at or below the critical dilution.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes when sub-lethal toxicity constitutes failure; interpretation of which endpoints count and how significance is demonstrated at or below critical dilution affects compliance comparisons.

candidates.exact_span:
c. This permit may be reopened to require WET limits, chemical specific effluent limits,
      additional testing, and/or other appropriate actions to address toxicity.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Indicates toxicity may currently be addressed through monitoring and reopening rather than fixed numeric WET limits; interpreting whether enforceable numeric limits are presently in effect versus report-only monitoring changes limit applicability and monitoring-obligation analysis.

candidates.exact_span:
The permittee shall repeat a test, including the control and all effluent dilutions, if the
      procedures and quality assurance requirements defined in the test methods or in this
      permit are not satisfied, including the following additional criteria:
candidates.computation_change_reason: Makes test validity conditional on procedural and QA satisfaction; interpreting when criteria are unsatisfied changes whether a result can be used for limit comparison or must be treated as missing/invalid evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Sampling Requirement *             Minimum of 3 samples             Minimum of 3 samples
candidates.computation_change_reason: Imposes a minimum sample count for toxicity testing; interpretation of how 'minimum of 3 samples' applies across species, events, or periods affects whether monitoring was required and whether fewer samples leave a missing-evidence or unresolved state.

candidates.exact_span: Holding time *                     36 hours for first use           36 hours for first use
candidates.computation_change_reason: Limits allowable holding time before first use; interpreting compliance with the 36-hour constraint affects whether reported results are valid for limit comparison or should be classified as inadequate or missing evidence.

candidates.exact_span:

candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets a control-survival threshold for acceptable tests; different interpretation of the ≥80% criterion or its application when failed changes whether results count toward limit exceedance or are treated as invalid/missing.

candidates.exact_span:
